entries.answer:
GPU architecture: Blackwell Ultra (dual‑die Blackwell)[1][2][3]
Transistor count: 208 billion transistors per GPU[2][1]
Manufacturing process: TSMC 4NP[1][2]
CUDA cores: 20,480+ per GPU[4][2]
Streaming multiprocessors: 160 SMs per GPU[4][2][1]
Tensor Cores: 640 fifth‑generation Tensor Cores per GPU[2]
VRAM: 288 GB HBM3e per GPU[3][5][1]
Usable VRAM figure often cited: ~270 GB usable per B300 GPU[6]
Memory bandwidth: 8.0 TB/s (8000 GB/s) per GPU[5][3][1]
HBM configuration: eight 12‑high HBM3e stacks, 8,192‑bit total memory interface[1]
Die‑to‑die interconnect: NV‑HBI at 10 TB/s between the two dies in a B300[2][1]
Peak dense FP4 Tensor Core performance: 15 PFLOPS per GPU[5][4][2]
Peak dense FP8 Tensor Core performance: 5–7 PFLOPS per GPU (5 PFLOPS in NVIDIA blog tables, 7 PFLOPS in independent spec sheets)[4][5][1][2]
Peak dense FP16 Tensor Core performance: 3.5 PFLOPS per GPU[5][4]
Sparse FP4 performance: up to 20 PFLOPS per GPU[1][2]
Sparse FP8 performance: up to 10 PFLOPS per GPU[2][1]
FP64 vector FMA throughput: about 1.3 TFLOPS per GPU[7][6]
NVLink generation: 5th‑generation NVLink 5 per GPU[3][5][2]
NVLink bandwidth per GPU: 1.8 TB/s bidirectional[3][4][2]
PCIe interface: PCIe Gen6 x16, ~256 GB/s bidirectional host‑to‑device bandwidth[6][1]
Grace CPU interconnect: NVLink‑C2C at 900 GB/s for Grace–B300 coupling[1]
Maximum board power / TDP: up to 1,400 W per B300 GPU (typical range 1,100–1,400 W depending on chassis)[4][2][1]
Decompression engine throughput: up to ~800 GB/s per GPU[1]
Multi‑Instance GPU (MIG) support: up to 2×140 GB, 4×70 GB, or 7×34 GB instances per GPU[1]
